output.brief:
The wrong expiry dates did not come from the operators or the printer firmware. The printer records show that from 4 Oct, the day after Regulatory Affairs entered a 36-month shelf life for Veltranol, every job received a 36-month value from PackBridge. Those jobs show no operator overrides. Before that date every job matched the batch record, including the jobs after the firmware change and the jobs set up by agency operators. The 36-month value was meant to apply only to lots made from March 2027, and the ERP still holds 24 months as the value in effect. So the line integration service sent the future value early, which contradicts the vendor's statement that it can't. Why it did this is not yet explained. The camera only checks the print against the job data, so it passed every faulty carton.

Do not discipline or remove the agency operators, and do not switch off the camera check. Instead:
1. Reset the Veltranol shelf-life records.
2. Hold every Veltranol lot packed since 4 Oct. That includes the two lots from Line 1 now in the warehouse.
3. Add a second-person check of printed expiry against the batch record at each setup.
4. Check retained cartons of the other products with October edits, especially the two with 2027 valid-from dates.
5. Press Corvane to explain how the future value reached the line.

I'm fairly confident in this. Whether other products are affected is still open.
